method: Read both complete acquired Markdown bodies and independently verify their SHA-256 against acquisition receipts; compare with the separately reviewed drift supplement
observations: Both bodies retain preview status, experimental CLI enablement, registered-name and input requirements, and conditional interactive run/authoring approvals.

Noninteractive execution denies permissions that cannot be automatically approved; no interactive prompt is promised. Repository-extension trust permits executable code and is separate from agent tool permissions.
Result-file output excludes run identity and progress. A failed, interrupted or paused invocation can leave old output intact; file existence alone is not fresh success evidence.
Machine-readable output can carry name, run ID and status, but still requires actual invocation/result verification. Definition creation and registration are explicitly separate from starting a run.
Shared personal/project extensions copy definitions rather than progress or history. Repository updates and extension reload/availability checks precede use of new shared definitions.
App monitoring applies only to local sessions. OTel spans depend on prior enablement and do not themselves certify final acceptance.
Saved completed steps can be reused only in resumable runs; unsaved work may repeat. Increased limits count previous usage, and canceled runs cannot resume.
Scheduling examples concern current-session prompts, not evidence of durable autonomous recurring execution or authorization to publish plugins.
The two complete bodies preserve the same reviewed operative instructions while internal links carry version-specific prefixes. Separate page IDs and digests are retained.
remaining: Independent atomic claim and omission reconciliation
Linked permission, authentication, extension, scheduling and telemetry references
